claims.statement: ATH-005 (CRITICAL) on CLIENT18 under account client18: Failed logon burst followed by successful authentication. 15 failed logons for 'client18' on CLIENT18 from 172.16.1.18 within 179s. A successful logon followed at 08:06:50, 30s after the last failure. This may indicate the credential was successfully guessed and the account is now compromised.

ATH-006 (HIGH) on CLIENT18 under account client18: Account authenticated from a host where it has no session. Account 'client18' authenticated to CLIENT18 from CLIENT17, but has no interactive session on CLIENT17 (observed owner(s): DWM-1, UMFD-0, UMFD-1, client17). Credential use originating from a host the account does not operate on is consistent with lateral movement using stolen credentials, though legitimate alternate-credential workflows produce the same pattern.

ATH-007 (HIGH) on CLIENT18 under account SYSTEM: Remote service execution (PsExec-style). The Service Control Manager started an interactive command interpreter. This pattern is consistent with remote command execution via a temporary service. Command output is redirected to the administrative share '\\127.0.0.1\ADMIN$', which is characteristic of remote execution frameworks collecting results over SMB.
Case CASE-001 links 3 finding(s) from ATH-005, ATH-006, ATH-007 across host(s) CLIENT17, CLIENT18 and account(s) SYSTEM, client18, citing 17 telemetry event(s).
Account 'SYSTEM' has 2371 authentication event(s) (0 failed, 2371 successful) across hosts CLIENT17, CLIENT18, from source(s) none resolved.
Account 'client18' has 18 authentication event(s) (15 failed, 3 successful) across hosts CLIENT18, from source(s) CLIENT17, CLIENT18.
T1021.002 (SMB/Windows Admin Shares) is catalogued under Lateral Movement and is mapped to this case by ATH-006, ATH-007.
T1078 (Valid Accounts) is catalogued under Persistence, Privilege Escalation, Initial Access, Stealth and is mapped to this case by ATH-005, ATH-006.
T1110.001 (Password Guessing) is catalogued under Credential Access and is mapped to this case by ATH-005.
T1569.002 (Service Execution) is catalogued under Execution and is mapped to this case by ATH-007.

The sequence of events suggests that an attacker guessed credentials for 'client18' on CLIENT18, subsequently used those compromised credentials to authenticate from CLIENT17 (lateral movement), and then leveraged SYSTEM privileges to execute remote commands via PsExec.
